name: Restraint Bias
description: People overestimate how well their future self will resist temptation or stay in control around triggers. Feeling strong now leads them to take exposure risks that make later self-control failures more likely.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to behavior-change, health, fintech, spending controls, parental controls, content safety, and any product that relies on users' future restraint. Good design often needs guardrails or precommitment, not just faith that users will resist later temptation.
prevalence_note: Known in self-control, addiction, and behavior-change literatures and occasionally useful in product work on guardrails or precommitment, but not a mainstream named concept in ordinary UX reviews.

findings.description: Across four studies, people overestimated their capacity for impulse control, and those inflated self-restraint beliefs led them to expose themselves more to temptation. Among recovering smokers, stronger restraint-bias beliefs predicted more temptation exposure and higher relapse rates four months later.
findings.source_title: The Restraint Bias: How the Illusion of Self-Restraint Promotes Impulsive Behavior
